name: Raw dog food
seoDesc: Raw dog food: work out dog's ideal body weight from the muscle meat and the bone. A free biology calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the muscle meat, the bone, the liver and the vegetables and the Raw dog food calculator solves for dog's ideal body weight. It suits an animal, a plant or a biological process whose scale you want to put into perspective. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Raw dog food calculator work?
sections.html:
The Raw dog food calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports dog's ideal body weight in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the life stage); then you type in the muscle meat (Daily raw food recommendations), the muscle meat (Daily raw food recommendations), the bone (Daily raw food recommendations) and the bone (Daily raw food recommendations).

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Raw dog food calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Dog's ideal body weight=required amount of food ÷ (life stage, age (months))
%=muscle meat ÷ required amount of food
%=bone ÷ required amount of food
%=liver ÷ required amount of food
Organ=required amount of food × %
%=vegetables ÷ required amount of food

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Time, opening in months
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Mass, opening in grams
  • Mass, opening in grams
  • %, opening in percent
  • Mass, opening in grams
  • %, opening in percent
  • Mass, opening in grams

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Raw dog food calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Supporting a lesson, a lecture or a field note
  • Comparing two organisms, populations or processes
  • Putting a biological quantity into a scale you can picture
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the muscle meat, the bone and the liver — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Raw dog food calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns dog's ideal body weight, derived from the muscle meat, the bone and the liver. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Raw dog food calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the muscle meat, the bone, the liver and the vegetables, which is 13 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter age (months) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Age (months) opens in months and the chip beside it offers 27 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (3 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Age (months) = 0 mos. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Raw dog food calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
